rationale: Both candidates recover the sole ground-truth concern (trust_remote_code breaking on kernels 0.13.x) and correctly note it was already fixed by 9947f414 in this PR's history. X delivers this cleanly alongside six other well-grounded, file/line-anchored findings, several verified by actually stubbing and running the code (cache dedup, lock release, kernels>=0.15 ValueError behavior), making it precise and highly actionable. Y buries the same trust_remote_code finding in ~6 near-duplicate 'Validated'/finding entries (likely a pipeline artifact), uses unusable path references like '?:34', and mixes in genuinely valuable content (the uncached-invalid-module bug, CI-path coverage gaps) with a lot of redundant noise that hurts both precision and actionability.
